entities.name: Donald J. Trump
entities.role: 45th and 47th President of the United States; owner of the Trump Organization (held via trust during presidencies).
entities.summary: Central subject. Business interests include branded real estate licensing, golf and hotel properties, and (from 2024) cryptocurrency ventures.

entities.name: Jared Kushner
entities.role: Son-in-law; Senior Adviser to the President 2017–2021; founder of Affinity Partners (2021); unpaid envoy in Gaza diplomacy (2025–).
entities.summary: Led the first administration's Middle East portfolio, including the 2019 economic plan and the Abraham Accords period. After leaving office he founded Affinity Partners, a private-equity firm funded mainly by Gulf sovereign investors.

entities.name: Ivanka Trump
entities.role: Daughter; Adviser to the President 2017–2021.
entities.summary: Filed public financial disclosures while serving; outside income reported jointly analysed with Jared Kushner's.

entities.name: Eric Trump
entities.role: Son; Executive Vice President, Trump Organization; World Liberty Financial co-founder.
entities.summary: Runs Trump Organization business including Gulf licensing deals; reported signatory of the 2025 World Liberty stake sale.

entities.name: Donald Trump Jr.
entities.role: Son; Executive Vice President, Trump Organization; World Liberty Financial co-founder.
entities.summary: Co-runs the Trump Organization; listed among World Liberty Financial's co-founders.

entities.name: Charles Kushner
entities.role: Jared Kushner's father; founder of Kushner Companies; co-founder of the Charles and Seryl Kushner Foundation.
entities.summary: Family business and foundation are documented separately from Jared Kushner's own holdings.

entities.name: Steve Witkoff
entities.role: Real-estate investor; US Special Envoy to the Middle East (2025–); World Liberty Financial co-founder with his sons.
entities.summary: Not a family member. Included because he is a business partner of the Trump family in World Liberty Financial while serving as a Middle East envoy.

entities.name: Zach Witkoff
entities.role: Son of Steve Witkoff; World Liberty Financial co-founder.
entities.summary: Announced in May 2025 that USD1 would settle MGX's investment in Binance.

entities.name: The Trump Organization
entities.role: Trump family holding company for real estate, licensing, golf and hospitality.
entities.summary: Licenses the Trump name to foreign developers who own and build the projects; the licensor earns fees rather than owning the buildings.

entities.name: World Liberty Financial (WLF)
entities.role: Cryptocurrency venture launched 2024; issuer of the WLFI token and USD1 stablecoin.
entities.summary: Co-founded by Trump family members and the Witkoffs. Trump-family entities (reported as DT Marks DEFI LLC) hold an equity and token interest.

entities.name: Affinity Partners
entities.role: Private-equity firm founded by Jared Kushner in 2021 (Miami).
entities.summary: Limited partners are reported to be predominantly Gulf sovereign wealth funds (Saudi PIF, Qatar's QIA, Abu Dhabi's Lunate). Investments include an Israeli insurer (Phoenix Financial) and a stake in the EA take-private consortium.

entities.name: Kushner Companies
entities.role: Kushner family real-estate company.
entities.summary: Jared Kushner was its CEO before 2017. Owned 666 Fifth Avenue from 2007 until the 2018 Brookfield transaction.

entities.name: Charles and Seryl Kushner Foundation
entities.role: Kushner family charitable foundation.
entities.summary: Tax filings show grants to US nonprofits supporting institutions in West Bank settlements.

entities.name: American Friends of Beit El Yeshiva
entities.role: US fundraising arm of a yeshiva in the Beit El settlement (West Bank).
entities.summary: David Friedman, later US ambassador to Israel, was its president when the Kushner foundation's grants were reported.

entities.name: Dar Global (Dar Al Arkan)
entities.role: London-listed international arm of Saudi developer Dar Al Arkan.
entities.summary: Trump Organization's main Gulf licensing partner since 2022 (Oman, Jeddah, Riyadh, Dubai, Qatar).

entities.name: Phoenix Financial
entities.role: Israeli insurance and investment group (publicly traded, Tel Aviv).
entities.summary: Affinity Partners became its largest shareholder in 2025. Its investment portfolio includes holdings in Israeli defense suppliers.

entities.name: Elbit Systems
entities.role: Israel's largest weapons manufacturer.
entities.summary: Appears here only as a Phoenix Financial portfolio holding identified by CNN; no direct Trump-family holding is documented.

entities.name: Menora Mivtachim
entities.role: Israeli insurer (publicly traded, Tel Aviv).
entities.summary: Invested in Kushner Companies apartment properties in 2017.

entities.name: Bank Hapoalim
entities.role: Israeli bank.
entities.summary: Reported lender to Kushner Companies.

entities.name: Brookfield (Brookfield Property Partners)
entities.role: Canadian asset manager.
entities.summary: Took a 99-year prepaid lease of 666 Fifth Avenue in 2018. The Qatar Investment Authority was a significant investor in Brookfield Property Partners.

entities.name: Electronic Arts (EA)
entities.role: US video-game publisher.
entities.summary: Agreed in September 2025 to a $55 billion take-private by PIF, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners.

entities.name: Silver Lake
entities.role: US private-equity firm.
entities.summary: Co-investor in the EA take-private.

entities.name: Binance
entities.role: Cryptocurrency exchange.
entities.summary: Received MGX's $2 billion minority investment, settled in WLF's USD1 stablecoin.

entities.name: LIV Golf
entities.role: Professional golf league backed by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund.
entities.summary: Has staged tournaments at Trump-owned golf courses since 2022.

entities.name: Crescent Heights
entities.role: US real-estate developer.
entities.summary: Trump's partner in a 2006 Ramat Gan (Israel) land purchase; later sued by the Trump Organization.

entities.name: Preserve America PAC
entities.role: Pro-Trump super PAC.
entities.summary: Principal recipient of Miriam Adelson's 2024 political contributions.

entities.name: Public Investment Fund (Saudi Arabia)
entities.role: Saudi sovereign wealth fund chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
entities.summary: Largest investor in Affinity Partners; LIV Golf's backer; lead investor in the EA take-private.

entities.name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
entities.role: Foreign government.
entities.summary: Payments by the Saudi government to Trump properties during 2017–2021 are documented in Mazars records cited by House Oversight Democrats.

entities.name: State of Qatar
entities.role: Foreign government.
entities.summary: Donor of a Boeing 747-8 to the US Department of Defense (2025); owner of Qatari Diar and the QIA.

entities.name: Qatar Investment Authority (QIA)
entities.role: Qatari sovereign wealth fund.
entities.summary: Affinity Partners limited partner (2024); investor in Brookfield Property Partners.

entities.name: Qatari Diar
entities.role: Real-estate company of Qatar's sovereign wealth fund.
entities.summary: Master developer of Simaisma, where a Trump-branded golf club and villas are planned with Dar Global.

entities.name: United Arab Emirates
entities.role: Foreign government.
entities.summary: Party to the Abraham Accords; home of MGX, Lunate and Aryam Investment.

entities.name: Lunate
entities.role: Abu Dhabi investment manager.
entities.summary: Affinity Partners limited partner (2024).

entities.name: MGX
entities.role: Abu Dhabi AI-focused investment firm chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed.
entities.summary: Invested $2 billion in Binance, settled in USD1.

entities.name: Aryam Investment 1
entities.role: Abu Dhabi entity reported to be backed by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed.
entities.summary: Reported buyer of a 49% stake in World Liberty Financial (WSJ).

entities.name: Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan
entities.role: UAE National Security Adviser; chairs MGX and G42.
entities.summary: Linked through MGX and Aryam to two transactions involving World Liberty Financial.

entities.name: Miriam Adelson
entities.role: Israeli-American billionaire and Republican donor.
entities.summary: Largest individual donor to pro-Trump super PAC spending in 2024.

entities.name: Sheldon Adelson (d. 2021)
entities.role: Casino magnate and Republican donor.
entities.summary: Reported in 2018 to have offered to fund part of the Jerusalem embassy.

entities.name: State of Israel (Government)
entities.role: Foreign government.
entities.summary: Counterparty to US recognition decisions, arms sales and peace initiatives; its regulator approved Affinity's Phoenix stake increase.

entities.name: US Department of State
entities.role: Executive department.
entities.summary: Issued the 2019 settlements legal position and 2025 emergency arms-sale determinations.

entities.name: US Department of Defense
entities.role: Executive department.
entities.summary: Formal recipient of Qatar's Boeing 747-8.

entities.name: Senate Finance Committee (Wyden)
entities.role: Congressional committee; Sen. Ron Wyden chair (2021–2025), then ranking member.
entities.summary: Ran an investigation into Affinity Partners' foreign funding and 666 Fifth Avenue.

entities.name: House Oversight Committee Democrats
entities.role: Minority staff of the House Committee on Oversight.
entities.summary: Authored the January 2024 report on foreign-government payments to Trump businesses; 2026 letters on Kushner.

entities.name: House Judiciary Committee Democrats (Raskin)
entities.role: Minority of the House Judiciary Committee.
entities.summary: Opened a 2026 inquiry into Affinity Partners and Kushner's envoy role.

entities.name: Jerusalem recognition & embassy relocation (2017–18)
entities.role: Proclamation 9683 (Dec 6, 2017); interim embassy opened May 2018.
entities.summary: Formal US recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital.

entities.name: Golan Heights recognition (2019)
entities.role: Proclamation 9852 (Mar 25, 2019).
entities.summary: US recognition of the Golan Heights as part of Israel.

entities.name: Settlements legal position (2019)
entities.role: Secretary Pompeo's statement of Nov 18, 2019.
entities.summary: The US stopped treating West Bank settlements as per se inconsistent with international law.

entities.name: "Peace to Prosperity" economic plan (2019–20)
entities.role: $50 billion proposed investment framework presented by Kushner, June 2019.
entities.summary: Proposal only; funders were not identified and it was conditional on a political settlement.

entities.name: Abraham Accords (2020)
entities.role: Normalization agreements signed at the White House, Sept 15, 2020.
entities.summary: Israel–UAE and Israel–Bahrain normalization, with the US as witness.

entities.name: Emergency arms sales to Israel (Feb 2025)
entities.role: Emergency determination bypassing congressional review.
entities.summary: Munitions and bulldozer sales totalling roughly $3 billion.

entities.name: 2016 US–Israel Memorandum of Understanding
entities.role: $38 billion military assistance framework, FY2019–2028 (signed under President Obama).
entities.summary: Context only. The baseline aid framework predates the Trump administration.

entities.name: Gaza "takeover" proposal (Feb 2025)
entities.role: Proposal announced at Feb 4, 2025 press conference.
entities.summary: Trump proposed US long-term ownership and redevelopment of Gaza.

entities.name: 20-point Gaza plan & Board of Peace (2025–26)
entities.role: White House plan of Sept 29, 2025; Board of Peace chaired by Trump.
entities.summary: Ceasefire and post-war governance framework; the Board oversees reconstruction funding.

entities.name: Acceptance of Qatari 747-8 (2025)
entities.role: Department of Defense acceptance, May 2025; MOU July 2025.
entities.summary: Aircraft accepted as a gift to the US government for conversion to presidential use.

claims.title: Trump recognized Jerusalem as Israel's capital and ordered the embassy moved
claims.statement: On December 6, 2017, President Trump signed Proclamation 9683 recognizing Jerusalem as the capital of Israel and directing the relocation of the US Embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem.
claims.limitations: Establishes the decision only. It says nothing about motive or about any financial benefit to anyone.

sources.quote: I have determined that it is time for the United States to officially recognize Jerusalem as the capital of Israel.

claims.title: The interim embassy in Jerusalem was scheduled to open on May 14, 2018
claims.statement: The State Department told Congress that an interim US embassy in Jerusalem, housed in an existing consular facility in the Arnona neighborhood, would open on May 14, 2018, coinciding with the 70th anniversary of Israel's independence.
claims.limitations: The sources here pre-date the opening and describe the plan. The opening itself is widely reported but is not separately sourced in this register.

claims.title: Sheldon Adelson reportedly offered to pay for part of the Jerusalem embassy
claims.statement: According to four US officials who spoke to the Associated Press in February 2018, the administration was weighing an offer from Republican donor Sheldon Adelson to pay for at least part of the new embassy in Jerusalem, and State Department lawyers were examining whether private donations could legally be accepted.
claims.limitations: Anonymous officials; a single originating report (AP). This register found no record of whether the offer was accepted or any money paid. An offer to fund a government building is not a payment to Trump.

sources.locator: AP report reproduced by News Tribune

claims.title: Trump recognized the Golan Heights as part of Israel
claims.statement: On March 25, 2019, President Trump signed Proclamation 9852 declaring that the United States recognizes the Golan Heights as part of the State of Israel.
claims.limitations: Establishes the decision only.

sources.quote: do hereby proclaim that, the United States recognizes that the Golan Heights are part of the State of Israel.

claims.title: Israel named a Golan community "Trump Heights" — no money involved
claims.statement: In June 2019 Israel's cabinet renamed the small Golan community of Bruchim (about ten residents) "Ramat Trump" ("Trump Heights") in appreciation of the Golan recognition. Trump publicly thanked Israel for "this great honor."
claims.limitations: A symbolic naming. No document reviewed shows any payment, licence fee, or property interest for Trump or his family.

claims.title: The US stopped calling West Bank settlements inconsistent with international law
claims.statement: On November 18, 2019, Secretary of State Mike Pompeo announced that the US would no longer follow a 1978 State Department legal opinion, and that establishing Israeli civilian settlements in the West Bank is "not per se inconsistent with international law." He said the US expressed no view on any individual settlement.
claims.limitations: The official state.gov transcript was not retrieved; the text is from a newspaper reproduction plus independent reporting.

claims.title: Kushner presented a $50 billion economic plan with no named funders
claims.statement: In June 2019 the White House, led by Jared Kushner, released the economic portion of its "Peace to Prosperity" plan, proposing about $50 billion of investment across the Palestinian territories, Egypt, Jordan and Lebanon. It was conditional on a political settlement and did not name its funders. Kushner said he hoped wealthy Gulf states, other countries and private investors would pay for much of it.
claims.limitations: A proposal, not a funded programme. No disbursement is documented here. The political portion (January 2020) is not separately sourced in this register.

claims.title: Israel, the UAE and Bahrain signed the Abraham Accords at the White House
claims.statement: On September 15, 2020, President Trump hosted a White House ceremony at which Israel, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain signed normalization agreements, with the US participating as a witness.
claims.limitations: The sources here do not describe Kushner's negotiating role, so it is not asserted. Later Gulf investments in Kushner's fund are documented separately (C-020, C-024); no document links them to the Accords.

claims.title: The 2016 aid agreement ($38 billion, FY2019–2028) predates Trump
claims.statement: The US and Israel signed their third 10-year military aid memorandum in 2016, under President Obama. It covers FY2019–FY2028 and totals $38 billion ($33 billion in Foreign Military Financing plus $5 billion for missile defense), subject to annual appropriations.
claims.limitations: Included as context. The baseline flow of US military aid to Israel during both Trump terms comes from an agreement signed before he took office, so it cannot be attributed to his decisions.

sources.quote: the United States pledged to provide—subject to congressional appropriation—$38 billion in military aid ($33 billion in Foreign Military Financing grants plus $5 billion in missile defense appropriations)

claims.title: The Trump administration fast-tracked roughly $3 billion in arms sales to Israel
claims.statement: On February 28, 2025, the State Department notified Congress of emergency sales to Israel, bypassing the usual congressional review. AP and CBS reported three components — bombs and warheads worth $2.04 billion, other munitions worth $675.7 million, and Caterpillar D9 bulldozers worth $295 million.
claims.limitations: The Arms Control Association describes an emergency declaration covering about $4 billion, which may be a different aggregate; the discrepancy is unresolved. These sales are paid for by Israel, including with US-funded FMF, and are not income to any Trump entity.

claims.title: Trump proposed a US "takeover" of Gaza and a "Riviera of the Middle East"
claims.statement: At a February 4, 2025 press conference with Benjamin Netanyahu, Trump proposed that the US take a long-term ownership position in Gaza, resettle its population elsewhere and lead its redevelopment, describing a possible "Riviera of the Middle East."
claims.limitations: A stated proposal. No document reviewed shows a Trump or family business interest in Gaza land or reconstruction contracts.

sources.locator: AP live coverage, Feb 4, 2025 ("long-term ownership position")

claims.title: The 20-point Gaza plan puts reconstruction funding under a Trump-chaired Board of Peace
claims.statement: The White House plan of September 29, 2025 provides for a ceasefire, hostage releases, a technocratic Palestinian committee to run Gaza, and a "Board of Peace" headed and chaired by President Trump that would set the framework for, and handle the funding of, Gaza's redevelopment.
claims.limitations: The whitehouse.gov original was not retrieved; the text comes from a full-text reprint. Chairing a body that controls funds is not, by itself, a financial benefit.

sources.locator: Reprint of plan text, point on the Board of Peace
The New Arab summary of plan

claims.title: A draft Board of Peace charter reportedly sets a $1 billion fee for permanent seats
claims.statement: AFP and NPR reported in January 2026 that a draft Board of Peace charter exempts states contributing more than $1 billion in cash in the first year from the three-year membership term and names Trump as chairman. The White House called reports about the fee "misleading."
claims.limitations: Based on a reported draft. This register has not seen the final charter or any record of payments. No evidence shows fees flowing to Trump personally.
claims.responses: The White House described reports about the fee as "misleading."

claims.title: Saudi Arabia's PIF committed $2 billion to Kushner's new fund
claims.statement: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund committed $2 billion to Affinity Partners, which Jared Kushner founded after leaving the White House. The New York Times reported (April 2022) that a PIF screening panel objected, citing inexperienced management and an "excessive" fee, and that the full board, chaired by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, approved it anyway. Senate Finance Chairman Wyden's 2024 letter refers to the PIF's "$2 billion in committed funds."
claims.limitations: A $2 billion commitment is investment capital managed by the fund, not money paid to Kushner. His personal income comes from fees and any profit share, which are not publicly broken out. The screening-panel detail rests on the NYT's reporting of internal documents.
claims.responses: Affinity's spokesperson said the firm is proud to count the PIF and other organisations with careful screening criteria among its investors.

sources.quote: charging its lead investor, the Saudi Public Investment Fund, a 1.25 percent annual fee on $2 billion in committed funds.

claims.title: Senate Finance Chairman says Affinity collected up to $157M in fees with no returns
claims.statement: According to Senate Finance Chairman Ron Wyden's September 25, 2024 letter, Affinity Partners had "pocketed as much as $157 million in fees from foreign clients, including $87 million from the Saudi government," and had generated no return on investment as of July 2024.
claims.limitations: The letter is verified; its figures are the committee's characterization from records it obtained, not audited accounts. "As much as" makes $157 million an upper bound. The $87 million is part of the $157 million and is not added to it. Fees are revenue to the firm, not Kushner's personal income.
claims.responses: This register has not retrieved a response from Affinity to the specific fee figures.

sources.quote: Affinity has pocketed as much as $157 million in fees from foreign clients, including $87 million from the Saudi government.

sources.locator: Boston Globe summary of the letter

claims.title: Wyden opened an inquiry into Gulf payments to Affinity and a possible FARA loophole
claims.statement: In June 2024 Senate Finance Chairman Wyden opened an inquiry into foreign payments to Affinity Partners, arguing that foreign-funded private funds could be used to avoid Foreign Agents Registration Act disclosure.
claims.limitations: An inquiry is not a finding of wrongdoing. No charge or adverse legal finding against Kushner is documented here.

claims.title: Wyden and Raskin asked DOJ for a special counsel on Kushner
claims.statement: On October 24, 2024, Sen. Ron Wyden and Rep. Jamie Raskin asked the Justice Department to appoint a special counsel to investigate whether Jared Kushner acted as an unregistered foreign agent.
claims.limitations: A request by opposition-party lawmakers. This register found no record of a special counsel being appointed.

claims.title: Qatar's QIA and Abu Dhabi's Lunate added $1.5 billion to Affinity in 2024
claims.statement: Affinity Partners took in an additional $1.5 billion from the Qatar Investment Authority and Abu Dhabi's Lunate, disclosed in December 2024. Kushner said the talks began in February 2024 and closed before the US election. Assets under management reached about $4.8 billion at the end of 2024, according to SEC filings cited by AGBI.
claims.limitations: Commitments to a fund are not income to its founder. The SEC Form ADV was not retrieved directly.
claims.responses: Kushner framed the raise as avoiding future conflicts, saying the firm would not need to raise capital for four years.

claims.title: Affinity became the largest shareholder of Israeli insurer Phoenix Financial
claims.statement: Affinity Partners bought 4.95% of Phoenix Financial in July 2024 (about NIS 466–470 million), with an option on another 4.95% at the same valuation. In January 2025, on the last day before the option expired, Israel's Capital Markets, Insurance and Savings Authority approved the exercise, taking Affinity to 9.9% and making it the largest shareholder, with voting rights capped at 5%.
claims.limitations: The regulatory approval itself was not retrieved. Calcalist reported the option exercise produced an "instant profit" of about $72 million on paper, which is unrealized appreciation, not cash.

claims.title: Affinity sold a quarter of its Phoenix stake for about NIS 1.05 billion
claims.statement: In July 2026 Affinity Partners sold about 2.5% of Phoenix Financial for roughly NIS 1.05 billion (about $343 million), cutting its stake from 9.9% to 7.4%. Its remaining stake was valued at about NIS 3.3 billion. Reports put the total gain on the original NIS 940 million investment at about NIS 3.4 billion.
claims.limitations: The NIS 3.4 billion "gain" combines realized proceeds with unrealized appreciation on the remaining shares, and accrues to the fund's investors as well as its manager. Kushner's personal share is not disclosed.

claims.title: CNN found Phoenix holds stakes in Israeli military suppliers; no direct link to diplomacy found
claims.statement: A CNN investigation (October 2026) reported that Phoenix Financial holds investments in at least nine suppliers to the Israeli military, the largest being about $265 million in Elbit Systems. Affinity owns none of the nine directly. CNN reported no direct link between Kushner's diplomacy and these investments.
claims.limitations: CNN's original article was not retrieved; its findings are known from other outlets' summaries. The exposure is indirect. Phoenix's portfolio decisions are made by Phoenix, not Affinity.
claims.responses: Kushner's attorney said he "never participated in or directed Phoenix's decisions" about the nine companies. Kushner called the story "deeply misleading," saying Phoenix is one of Israel's largest publicly traded financial institutions, not a defense company.

claims.title: House Oversight's top Democrat sought answers on Kushner's Phoenix stake
claims.statement: On October 6, 2026, Rep. Robert Garcia, ranking member of the House Oversight Committee, wrote to Affinity Partners seeking information following CNN's reporting on its Phoenix Financial stake.
claims.limitations: A minority-party letter; no finding.
claims.responses: Kushner's lawyer noted that Garcia himself has pension interests in Phoenix and Elbit. Garcia's office said those pensions are managed by state systems.

claims.title: Kushner negotiated the Gaza ceasefire as an unpaid envoy while Gulf states fund his firm
claims.statement: Kushner was sent to Sharm el-Sheikh in October 2025 to help seal the Gaza ceasefire. Several regional governments he negotiated with are investors in Affinity Partners. CNN reported that, as an unpaid envoy rather than a formal official, he was not required to file a public financial disclosure.
claims.limitations: The overlap of roles is documented. No evidence reviewed shows a specific negotiating position taken to benefit Affinity.
claims.responses: The White House said Kushner's business has nothing to do with his diplomacy, which he conducts as a volunteer; press secretary Karoline Leavitt called the criticism "frankly despicable." Kushner has argued that business ties can bring Israelis and Arabs together.

sources.locator: Arab News summary of CNN (disclosure point)

claims.title: PIF, Silver Lake and Affinity agreed to buy EA for $55 billion
claims.statement: On September 29, 2025, Electronic Arts agreed to be acquired by a consortium of Saudi Arabia's PIF, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners at an enterprise value of about $55 billion ($210 per share in cash). PIF would roll over its existing 9.9% stake.
claims.limitations: $55 billion is the deal's enterprise value, not Affinity's investment. Affinity's equity share was not found. This register has not confirmed whether the deal has closed.

claims.title: Raskin says Affinity has $6.16 billion under management, 99% foreign-funded
claims.statement: In April 2026 Rep. Jamie Raskin (House Judiciary ranking member) opened an inquiry into Kushner's dual roles. His letter states that Affinity has about $6.16 billion in assets under management, 99% from foreign nationals including the Saudi, UAE and Qatari sovereign funds. In August 2026 he expanded the probe to a planned $120 million resort in Albania.
claims.limitations: The $6.16 billion and 99% figures are the letter's characterization; the underlying filings were not retrieved. Kushner did not respond to the committee, per Raskin.

sources.locator: House Judiciary Democrats press release, Aug 2026

claims.title: Democrats say Kushner sought $5 billion in new foreign capital while serving as envoy
claims.statement: In March 2026 Sen. Wyden and Rep. Garcia wrote to the White House and Affinity Partners, citing reporting that Kushner was seeking to raise at least $5 billion in additional foreign capital while serving as an envoy.
claims.limitations: The fundraising figure rests on media reporting cited by the lawmakers, and Affinity disputes it.
claims.responses: Affinity's chief legal officer said the firm has had only early-stage talks about additional fundraising and does not plan to accept new capital while Kushner volunteers for the government.

sources.locator: NYT report reposted by Rep. Garcia

claims.title: Kushner called Gaza's waterfront "very valuable" in a 2024 interview
claims.statement: In a February 15, 2024 interview at Harvard's Middle East Initiative, made public in March 2024, Kushner said "Gaza's waterfront property, it could be very valuable" and said that, from Israel's perspective, he would do his best to move people out and then clean the area up.
claims.limitations: A statement of opinion by a private citizen at the time. No document reviewed shows any Affinity or Kushner investment in Gaza property.
claims.responses: Kushner said on X that he stood by his comments and posted the full interview.

claims.title: CREW put Jared and Ivanka's White House-era outside income at $172M–$640M
claims.statement: CREW's February 2021 analysis of their financial disclosures found that Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump reported between $172 million and $640 million in outside income while working in the White House.
claims.limitations: The range is wide because disclosures report income in broad bands. Lead Stories notes that $640 million is the upper bound, not a confirmed total. The figure is not specific to Israel or the Gulf.

sources.quote: Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump reported between $172 million and $640 million in outside income while working in the White House, according to an analysis of financial disclosures by CREW.

sources.locator: Fact check on the upper bound

claims.title: An Israeli insurer invested about $30M in Kushner family properties in 2017
claims.statement: The New York Times reported (January 2018) that Israeli insurer Menora Mivtachim invested about $30 million in Kushner Companies' Maryland apartment complexes in 2017, and that Kushner Companies had taken at least four loans from Bank Hapoalim.
claims.limitations: Known through JTA's summary of the NYT; the original was not retrieved. The Times reported that the deal did not involve Jared Kushner personally and did not violate federal ethics law.
claims.responses: Menora's real-estate head said the deal was unaffected by Kushner's government role.

claims.title: The Brookfield lease that rescued 666 Fifth Avenue — the Qatar link is disputed
claims.statement: In 2018 Brookfield took a 99-year lease on Kushner Companies' 666 Fifth Avenue and prepaid the rent for the full term, about $1.1–1.3 billion by various accounts, which let the Kushners clear the building's mortgage. The Qatar Investment Authority was a major investor in Brookfield Property Partners. Sen. Wyden and Rep. Joaquin Castro investigated whether the deal influenced US policy toward Qatar.
claims.limitations: The reported lease value varies by source. A link between QIA money and the lease is contested.
claims.responses: Brookfield said the QIA was not involved and that it had no obligation to inform the QIA. Per Wyden's office, Brookfield twice declined to provide requested information.

claims.title: The Kushner family foundation gave to a settlement yeshiva's US fundraising arm
claims.statement: Tax filings analysed by Haaretz show the Charles and Seryl Kushner Foundation gave at least $38,000 to American Friends of Beit El Yeshiva between 2011 and 2013. The group's president at the time was David Friedman, later US ambassador to Israel.
claims.limitations: Both outlets restate Haaretz's analysis of the tax filings; the filings were not retrieved. Charitable giving by the family foundation, legal and tax-exempt under US law. It is money flowing out of the family, not a benefit to it, and it predates the presidency.
claims.responses: A Kushner Companies spokesperson declined to comment.

claims.title: House Democrats documented at least $7.8M from foreign governments to Trump businesses
claims.statement: A January 2024 report by House Oversight Committee Democratic staff, based on Mazars accounting records, identified at least $7.8 million paid by at least 20 foreign governments to four Trump-owned businesses during his first term, including $615,422 from Saudi Arabia and $465,744 from Qatar.
claims.limitations: A minority staff report covering only 4 of more than 500 Trump businesses, so the total is a floor. It is revenue (e.g. hotel bills), not profit. The report PDF was not retrieved; figures are from AP and the Boston Globe.
claims.responses: This register did not find a Trump Organization response to the specific figures.

claims.title: Saudi developer Dar Global licenses the Trump brand across the Gulf
claims.statement: Dar Global, the international arm of Saudi developer Dar Al Arkan, has licensed the Trump brand for projects in Oman (signed 2022), Jeddah (Trump Tower, December 2024), Riyadh (two projects, December 2024), Dubai (announced 2024) and a $1 billion Trump Plaza in Jeddah (September 2025). Under these deals Dar Global owns and develops the projects and the Trump Organization licenses the name.
claims.limitations: Project values are developer figures, not Trump income. Licence fee terms are not public.

claims.title: Trump reported about $21.9M in licence fees from Dar Al Arkan in one year
claims.statement: Press accounts of Trump's financial disclosures report about $21.9 million in licence fees from Dar Al Arkan in 2024, and $5.35 million in licence fees for the Oman project in 2022. Forbes reported $7.85 million from the Oman project between 2021 and early 2024.
claims.limitations: The OGE Form 278e filings were not retrieved, so figures come from secondary reporting that differs by year and project. Licence fees are revenue; profit is not disclosed.

claims.title: Qatar's state developer signed for a Trump-branded golf resort near Doha
claims.statement: On April 30, 2025, Qatari Diar, the real-estate arm of Qatar's sovereign wealth fund, signed an agreement with Dar Global to develop the Trump International Golf Club and Trump-branded villas at its Simaisma project north of Doha. Eric Trump attended the signing. The National reported a $5.25 million licence fee to Trump connected to the project.
claims.limitations: The agreement is corroborated; the $5.25 million fee comes from a single outlet. A reported ~$3 billion project cost is a single-source figure and is not used. The Trump Organization's own release could not be retrieved (HTTP 403).

claims.title: The Pentagon accepted a Boeing 747-8 from Qatar
claims.statement: The Department of Defense accepted a Boeing 747-8 from Qatar in May 2025 for conversion to presidential use. An MOU signed in July 2025 describes it as a "bona fide gift" to the Department, at no cost to the US. ABC News reported that the terms allow Trump to use the plane after leaving office. The aircraft is commonly valued at about $400 million; the refit cost was not disclosed.
claims.limitations: The gift was made to the US government, not to Trump personally. Post-presidency use is reported second-hand. The $400 million value is an estimate.
claims.responses: The Pentagon said acceptance followed all federal rules and regulations.

claims.title: Trump disclosed $57.35M from World Liberty token sales for 2024
claims.statement: Trump's financial disclosure covering 2024, filed in June 2025, reported about $57.35 million in income from World Liberty Financial token sales.
claims.limitations: The OGE filing was not retrieved directly. The income is not tied to Israel policy.

claims.title: Trump's 2025 disclosure reported roughly $1.4 billion in crypto income
claims.statement: Trump's disclosure covering 2025, filed in 2026, reported roughly $1.4 billion in cryptocurrency-linked income according to PolitiFact, including about $791 million tied to World Liberty Financial and about $635 million from a Celebration Coins (meme-coin) licensing arrangement. InvestmentNews calculated about $592 million in WLF-linked proceeds.
claims.limitations: Outlets disagree on totals ($592–800 million for WLF) depending on what they count. The 927-page filing was not retrieved.
claims.responses: Deputy press secretary Anna Kelly said neither the president nor his family would engage in conflicts of interest.

claims.title: Abu Dhabi's MGX settled a $2 billion Binance investment in WLF's USD1 stablecoin
claims.statement: MGX, the Abu Dhabi firm chaired by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed, agreed in March 2025 to invest $2 billion in Binance. In May 2025, WLF co-founder Zach Witkoff announced that the deal would be settled in WLF's USD1 stablecoin.
claims.limitations: The $2 billion went to Binance, not WLF. How much WLF earns from the stablecoin's reserves is not documented, so the benefit to WLF is inferred, not measured.

claims.title: WSJ — a Tahnoon-backed firm bought 49% of World Liberty days before the inauguration
claims.statement: The Wall Street Journal reported that Aryam Investment 1, an Abu Dhabi entity backed by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed, agreed to buy 49% of World Liberty Financial for $500 million in an agreement signed in January 2025, four days before the inauguration. Half was reportedly paid upfront, with about $187 million going to Trump family-controlled entities and at least $31 million to entities affiliated with the Witkoff family.
claims.limitations: Single originating outlet (WSJ), known here through The Block and Ledger Insights. The WSJ article was not retrieved. Details of the payment split vary slightly between summaries.

claims.title: Envoy Witkoff kept a World Liberty interest despite a divestment pledge
claims.statement: Bloomberg reported that Steve Witkoff, the US Special Envoy to the Middle East, still held a financial interest in World Liberty Financial according to his August 2025 disclosure, despite saying in March 2025 that he was divesting and transferring the holdings to his sons.
claims.limitations: Witkoff is not a Trump family member. The disclosure did not show whether ethics officials approved his divestiture plan.

claims.title: Miriam Adelson gave about $100 million to a pro-Trump super PAC in 2024
claims.statement: According to FEC filings as reported, Miriam Adelson contributed about $100 million to Preserve America PAC, a pro-Trump super PAC, in 2024, with $95 million reported in the third quarter alone.
claims.limitations: A political contribution to an independent-expenditure committee is not income to Trump. The FEC filing itself was not retrieved. No document reviewed links the contributions to a specific policy decision.

claims.title: Saudi-backed LIV Golf has played at a Trump course every season since 2022
claims.statement: LIV Golf, backed by Saudi Arabia's PIF, has held at least one event at a Trump-owned course each season since 2022. LIV payments are not separately itemized in Trump's disclosure; Trump has called the amount "peanuts," saying "They pay a rental fee."
claims.limitations: The amount paid is unknown. Club revenue figures (e.g. Doral's $121.8 million in 2025) cover all business, not LIV.

claims.title: Forbes estimates of Trump's net worth rose sharply after 2024
claims.statement: Forbes estimates of Trump's net worth, as reported, rose from about $3.9–4.3 billion in 2024 to $7.3 billion in September 2025, with crypto ventures adding an estimated $2 billion. A July 2026 AP report cited a Forbes estimate of $6 billion.
claims.limitations: These are third-party estimates, not disclosures, and the reported baselines conflict. Changes in net worth reflect market prices (e.g. token valuations), not realized income, and are not attributable to Israel policy.

claims.title: A Trump-licensed tower in Ramat Gan, Israel, was never built
claims.statement: In 2006 the Trump group and Crescent Heights bought a lot at Elite Junction in Ramat Gan, Israel, for about $44 million, intending a "Trump Plaza" tower. The Trump Organization later sued Crescent Heights over the project, and the tower was never built under the Trump name.
claims.limitations: Predates Trump's political career. The lawsuit's outcome was not found. It is listed because it is the only Trump-branded Israeli property project found in this research.

claims.title: Inference: Gulf states are both deal counterparties and diplomatic counterparts
claims.statement: The record shows the same Gulf sovereign actors (Saudi Arabia's PIF, Qatar's QIA and Qatari Diar, and Abu Dhabi entities linked to Sheikh Tahnoon) as counterparties in Trump-family business (Affinity capital, Trump licensing, the World Liberty stake) and as parties to US Middle East diplomacy in which Trump, Kushner and Witkoff are principals. This creates documented conflict-of-interest exposure. The evidence reviewed does not show that any specific US decision on Israel was made because of these financial relationships.
claims.limitations: An interpretation of documented facts. Causation is not established, and much US Gulf policy had other stated rationales.

claims.title: Inference: no financial link to Trump found for the Jerusalem, Golan or settlement decisions
claims.statement: This research found no document linking the Jerusalem recognition, the Golan recognition or the 2019 settlements position to a payment, investment or licence benefiting Trump or his family. The largest documented money associated with pro-Israel advocacy around Trump is political contributions (for example Miriam Adelson's ~$100 million in 2024), which are not personal income.
claims.limitations: Absence of evidence within this register's search scope is not proof of absence. Political contributions can create influence without personal enrichment; this register makes no finding on influence.

claims.title: Inference: Kushner's fund gained indirect exposure to Israeli defense-sector performance
claims.statement: Through its Phoenix Financial stake, Affinity Partners holds indirect exposure to Phoenix's portfolio, which includes Israeli defense suppliers. Phoenix's value rose substantially while Kushner was involved in Gaza diplomacy (C-026, C-029). Whether any diplomatic action affected that value is not established.
claims.limitations: Phoenix's share price is driven by many factors, including Israeli market performance generally. The amount of exposure attributable to defense holdings is not calculated here.
